workstream: WS3 - error structure by chemical bond class and structural environment

labeler_agreement.statement: the RDKit radical-centre labeler reproduces the database bond_type on all 331 matched benchmark rows

coverage.headline: The 543-observation benchmark contains only 3 of the 9 bond classes present in the database: C-H (302), C-C (240) and H-O (1). Every other class (C-N, C-O, H-N, N-N, N-O, O-O) is ABSENT (n=0), so no class-level error claim can be made for them.

ch1_error_by_bond_class.interpretation: Only C-H (n=302) and C-C (n=240) support a per-class MAE. H-O has n=1 and is reported for completeness only - no inference. The six other database classes have n=0 in the benchmark.

variance_decomposition_abs_err.note: OLS R^2 on |error|, 543 bond observations, one dummy for C-C vs C-H.

ch2_class_vs_size.answer: Formula for the verdict is in the narrative field; see 'verdict' below.

magnitude_size_confound.verdict: The weak-bond bin has ZERO observations with HAC<=5 and is shifted to larger parents (median HAC 12.5 vs 8.0 overall), so 'weak bond' and 'large molecule' cannot be separated across the sample as a whole. The one cell with enough weak-bond rows to test the magnitude effect with BOTH class and size held fixed is C-C / HAC>=10 (n_weak=12 vs n_rest=34); there the effect survives.

applicability_boundary.statement: Applicability boundary from the measured sample: all three channels are evaluated here only on C-H and C-C bonds. Within that domain the dominant failure axis is bond strength, not bond class. Below 70 kcal/mol (n=18 bond observations, mean experimental BDE 59.9) MAE rises to 5.9967 (quantum), 7.5267 (learned), 7.9389 (reference) kcal/mol, i.e. 3.0x / 3.2x / 1.5x the pooled MAE, with a large positive bias (quantum +4.57, learned +6.87). In the 85-100 kcal/mol window (n=210) quantum and learned are near-unbiased (MAE 1.6696 / 1.6382, bias +0.10 / +0.19).

narrative: Overall (543 bond observations): quantum MAE 2.0978 kcal/mol (bias +0.554), learned MAE 2.4107 (bias +1.079), reference MAE 5.486 (bias +1.378). Bond-class coverage is the binding constraint: C-H n=302, C-C n=240, H-O n=1, and C-N/C-O/H-N/N-N/N-O/O-O are entirely absent from the benchmark although they make up 16.5% of the database rows; no class-level claim can be made for those six classes. C-H vs C-C MAE: quantum 1.9907 vs 2.2345, learned 2.5416 vs 2.2365, reference 5.7109 vs 5.225 kcal/mol. The pooled C-H/C-C gaps are not stable effects: quantum and reference bootstrap 95% CIs span zero, and the C-H-vs-C-C direction itself FLIPS between size bins - among HAC<=5 parents C-C is better for quantum (1.61 vs 1.76), while among HAC>=10 parents C-H is better (2.20 vs 3.82, Mann-Whitney p=0.005). That is an interaction, not a class main effect. The C-H group is the larger-molecule group (median HAC 9.0 vs 7.0, Mann-Whitney p<1e-8), so class and size are partly confounded. quantum: R2(size only)=0.04561, R2(class only)=0.00298, R2(size+class)=0.06022 -> verdict 'size dominates' (incremental R2 from class given size = 0.01461). learned: R2(size only)=0.18176, R2(class only)=0.00327, R2(size+class)=0.18635 -> verdict 'size dominates' (incremental R2 from class given size = 0.0046). reference: R2(size only)=0.02979, R2(class only)=0.00346, R2(size+class)=0.02988 -> verdict 'size dominates' (incremental R2 from class given size = 0.0001). Error grows toward the weak-bond end for every channel: quantum Spearman |err| vs exp BDE rho=-0.1478 (p=0.00055), learned rho=-0.2522, reference rho=-0.1223. Levene p across experimental-magnitude bins: quantum 0.0, learned 0.0, reference 5.7e-05 - error is strongly heteroscedastic in bond strength. The reference channel is the one real class effect found: its bias flips sign between classes, +5.103 kcal/mol on C-H versus -3.303 on C-C (Welch p=0.0). It systematically over-estimates C-H bonds and under-estimates C-C bonds, and this is why its pooled MAE (5.49) is 2.6x the quantum channel's despite a similar RMSE. The learned channel's largest single environment effect is nitrogen: MAE 4.9024 on N-containing parents (n=37) versus 2.2285 otherwise (bootstrap 95% CI of the difference [1.3195, 4.061]), a 2.2x degradation. Within C-H bonds alone it is still 4.551 vs 2.3117, so it is not a class artifact. Ring/aromatic environment also matters for the learned channel: benzene-containing parents MAE 3.1952 (n=220) versus 1.8763 (n=323), and a ring-member radical centre gives the same direction (in-ring 3.0956 vs not 2.0625). The quantum channel shows the same direction more weakly, and the reference channel is largely flat to aromaticity. Size and bond strength are themselves confounded: the <70 kcal/mol bin contains no HAC<=5 observation at all and is shifted to larger parents (median HAC 12.5 vs 8.0 overall), so the 'large molecule' and 'weak bond' failure modes cannot be separated globally. The one cell with enough weak-bond rows to hold class and size fixed is C-C / HAC>=10 (12 weak vs 34 other): there quantum MAE is 7.66 vs 2.47 and learned 9.27 vs 2.51, so the magnitude effect does survive that control. That same cell, C-C / HAC>=10 / <70 kcal/mol, is the worst 3-way cell for both quantum and learned (n=12).
caveats: The benchmark's 543 rows are 543 heterogeneous literature bond observations, not independent repeats; experimental reference uncertainty is not propagated.
Only C-H and C-C are populated (plus a single H-O row): six of the nine database bond classes have zero benchmark coverage, so class-level error claims exist only for C-H vs C-C.
Unique molecules (419) and unique fragment pairs (543) are different analysis units from the 543 bond observations; per-class n values above count bond observations.
OLS R^2 on |error| is descriptive; the residual distribution is skewed and heteroscedastic, so R^2 magnitudes are small and should not be read as a predictive model.
Environment flags (aromaticity, ring membership, N/O content) are correlated with each other and with parent size; the stratified tables control only one factor at a time.
